blocks.html:
Templar

Role: Tank. Difficulty: Beginner friendly to pick up, but more gear dependent than it looks. Weapon: one handed sword or mace plus shield.

TankMeleeBeginner friendly

blocks.title: Overview and role
blocks.bodyHtml:
Templar tanks with a sword or mace and shield, built for threat control and mitigation, not damage.

AION 2's dedicated main tank fights in heavy armor with a one handed longsword or mace plus shield; a greatsword sometimes serves as an off-spec backup weapon fextralife, date unknown1 aion2hub, date unknown2.

Kit size

AION2 Hub lists 31 active skills and 10 passives single source aion2hub, date unknown3, while a separate guide counts 43 total, 33 active and 9 passive contested gamesolusi, 2026-074. The gap likely comes from counting rank-up versions of the same skill differently, so treat exact skill counts as approximate.

Role and difficulty

  • Built around threat generation, target lockdown, and damage mitigation, not damage output confirmed, multiple guides aion2hub, date unknown5 pvpbank, date unknown6
  • Rated beginner friendly for its durability, but more gear dependent than it looks: mastery points and defensive stats have an outsized effect on performance single source pvpbank, date unknown7

PvE and PvP standing

  • kr-era PvE (KR/TW meta): dominates dungeon tanking and holds its own solo, but has the lowest damage of the melee/DPS classes single source pvpbank, date unknown8
    • Gladiator, Assassin, and Sorcerer all out-damage it; solo leveling can feel slow without optimized skills and gear
  • PvP: scales well into organized, large-scale fights as a durable frontline initiator that absorbs pressure and disrupts enemy formations pvpbank, date unknown9

Who plays it

As the primary tank archetype, Templar is near-mandatory for structured group PvE, one of the safer "always wanted" picks for dungeon groups. No source gives a hard queue-time or demand statistic for this; treat it as inferred from role framing, not a documented fact.

Best for players who want to anchor the party, enjoy active threat and cooldown management over burst damage, and are willing to invest in gear and mastery to stay relevant confirmed, multiple guides aion2hub, date unknown10 pvpbank, date unknown11

blocks.title: Skill priority
blocks.headExtrasHtml: single source, assembled kr-era marketing-heavy
blocks.bodyHtml:
Level Vicious Strike, Provoke, and Doom Shield first to build threat and survive bursts.

No single guide gives a definitive numbered Skill Point leveling order for Templar, unlike the more detailed Gladiator guides. The list below is assembled from pieces documented across sources; treat it as single source or contested unless noted.

Core priority

  1. Do first: chain Vicious Strike to build and hold aggro, your bread-and-butter threat generator confirmed aion2hub, date unknown1 aoeah, 2025-112.
  2. Do first: Provoke, a single-target taunt used to lock a boss's aggro onto yourself confirmed aion2hub, date unknown3 aoeah, 2025-114.
  3. Do first: Doom Shield, a defensive and mitigation cooldown, timed against confirmed incoming burst rather than used on cooldown confirmed aion2hub, date unknown5 aoeah, 2025-116.
  4. Then: Punishment and Decisive Strike, hard-hitting follow-ups used once a target is locked down. Punishment is also described elsewhere as a chargeable AoE with lifesteal in an endgame raid-tank build single source aoeah, 2025-117.
  5. Then, for mob packs: Flash Cut (2s cooldown, hits 3 targets, usable while moving) triggers Bloodsword Slash, which heals for 100% of damage dealt single source pvpbank, date unknown8 aoeah, 2025-119.
  6. Then, for mob packs: Trial (also called Falling Sword Spirits) hits up to 6 targets and reduces their defense by 30% single source pvpbank, date unknown10.
  7. Then, for mob packs: Shield Strike grants a shield and heals more the more enemies it hits single source pvpbank, date unknown11.
  8. Then: Capture pulls a target up to 20m in and binds it 2 to 3 seconds, with a 100% bind chance on NPCs, good for consolidating scattered mobs before an AoE mitigation skill single source (community synthesis, no direct link)
  9. Later / optional: fund whichever mitigation or taunt skill you actually have equipped in your active rotation over situational or off-role skills; no source names specific Templar skills to ignore early expcarry, date unknown12.

Passive priority (contested)

contested, KR-era, single source A Korean forum post about 수호성 (Templar) passives gives two competing rankings for five named passives: 격앙 (Fury), 모욕의 포효 (Roar of Insult), 충격 적중 (Impact Hit), 체력 강화 (HP boost), 단죄의 가호 (Judgment's Grace), and 철벽 방어 (Iron Wall Defense).

  • By felt or practical value: Fury > Roar of Insult > Impact Hit, with the rest called not worth investing in
  • By raw combat-power-per-level the order flips: Iron Wall Defense (+0.356k) > Impact Hit (+0.244k) > HP boost (+0.233k) > Judgment's Grace (+0.111k) > Fury (+0.078k); Fury's felt value beats its CP number fmkorea, date unknown13
  • A second, independent KR guide broadly agrees on prioritizing core damage or defense passives over utility ones, but does not give the same explicit order single source vortexgaming, date unknown14
Gap remains: the two rankings above disagree with each other (felt value vs. raw CP-per-level), and neither maps cleanly onto the English passive names used elsewhere on this page, so treat this as a starting point, not a settled order.

Additional named actives seen in class-overview listings, priority unconfirmed, listed for reference only: Ferocious Strike, Pummel, Poach, Shield Smite, Judgment, Flash Rampage, Debilitating Smash, Warding Strike, Shield Rush, Annihilate, Defiance, Shield of Protection, Second Skin, Armor of Balance, Grapple fextralife, date unknown15.

blocks.title: Leveling build
blocks.headExtrasHtml: Lv 1 to cap contested kr-era
blocks.bodyHtml:
Push both basics to skill Lv 8, add Flash Assault at Lv 16, then bank Stigma Shards into Nezakan's Shield or Shield of Protection at Lv 23.

This order comes from Korean 수호성 community boards (mainly Inven), a Vortex Gaming PVE guide, a DCInside write-up, and the monotrees blog; no source gives a clean numbered table like a maxroll guide. Most steps use the skill's own level (8/12/16/20 breakpoints), not your character level, except where a step names one.

Skill point order

StepWhenSkillTake toWhySrc
1From Lv 1Fierce Strike (맹렬한 일격) and Consecutive Strikes (연속 난타)Skill Lv 8basics carry damage between cooldownsinven 130, 2025-11
2Alongside step 1Shield Bash (방패 강타), Guardian Strike (비호의 일격), Punishment (징벌)~Skill Lv 7-8core active rotation alongside the basicsinven 130, 2025-11
3Character Lv 25Fierce Strike and Consecutive Strikes againSkill Lv 12second specialization breakpointinven 93, date unknown
4Character Lv 12+Punishment (min. Lv 12), Consecutive StrikesSkill Lv 16-20most granular min/recommended levels founddcinside, 2026-07
5Character Lv 16+Flash Assault (섬광난무)Skill Lv 16+cuts all cooldowns 3s on hit, priority pickinven 354, 2025-11
6Character Lv 16+Weakness Strike (쇠약의 맹타)Skill Lv 16+payoff of the Shield Bash plus Guardian Strike comboinven 131, date unknown
7Toward Skill Lv 20, no character Lv givenFierce Strike, Consecutive Strikes, Judgment (심판), PunishmentSkill Lv 20Judgment alone credited with ~65% of PVE damagedcinside, 2026-07
8OngoingCapture (포획), Shock Release (충격 해제), Annihilation (섬멸)minimumcalled low-value versus the core rotationinven 130, 2025-11

No skill is singled out to leave at level 1; low-value skills instead get minimum ongoing investment, covered in step 8 above.

Passives

Two competing orders turned up for Templar's passives; neither could be reconciled, so both are given.

Order A: survivability first

  1. First: Health Reinforcement (체력 강화), flat HP inven 516, 2025-111
  2. Then: Iron Wall Defense (철벽 방어) and Guardian's Seal (수호의 인장) inven 516, 2025-112
  3. Later: Fervor (격앙), Condemnation's Protection (단죄의 가호), Taunt passive (모욕의 포효, later for PvP), Shock Hit (충격 적중), Pain Block, Survival Will inven 516, 2025-113

Cdia's guide, Nov 2025.

Order B: damage-buff first

  1. First: Fervor / Enrage (격앙): 0.3% self and 0.8% party damage per level, plus a 1.5x multiplier from the Virtuous Armor Stigma dcinside, 2026-074
  2. Then: Taunt passive (모욕의 포효): ~0.5% attack power per level, also boosted by Virtuous Armor dcinside, 2026-075
  3. Then: Shock Hit (충격 적중): 0.3% knockdown damage per level dcinside, 2026-076
  4. Later: Condemnation's Protection, Iron Wall Defense, Health Reinforcement dcinside, 2026-077

DCInside PVE guide, mid-2026, corroborated by a search snippet aggregating other Inven threads (single unverified source, no direct link).

Order B is more recent, with per-level percentages and an explicit Virtuous Armor synergy reason, while Order A is from KR launch week with no numbers. Lean toward Order B, but as a tank, do not skip Iron Wall Defense and Health Reinforcement entirely while leveling solo dcinside, 2026-078.

Level by level

  1. Lv 1-12
    Basics only: push Fierce Strike and Consecutive Strikes to skill Lv 8

    Weave in Shield Bash whenever it is off cooldown.

    • Alternate the two basics as your main loop, since specialization from skill Lv 8 depends on both inven 130, 2025-119
    • Shield Bash is used most often thanks to its short cooldown inven 6625, 2026-0410
  2. Lv 12-16
    Punishment and Guardian Strike come online

    Use Guardian Strike's damage-resistance window defensively, not just for damage inven 131, date unknown11.

    • Also bring Shield Bash, Guardian Strike, and Punishment to around skill Lv 7-8 alongside the basics inven 130, 2025-1112
  3. Lv 16
    Flash Assault and Weakness Strike unlock; get both moving fast

    Flash Assault cuts all other cooldowns by 3 seconds on hit, framed as the Templar's defining mechanic inven 354, 2025-1113.

    • Chain Shield Bash into Guardian Strike to trigger Weakness Strike, a debuff the whole kit benefits from inven 131, date unknown14
  4. Lv 23
    Stigma: two sources disagree on the first pick

    Nezakan's Shield is picked first, leveled to 15, for party survivability monotrees, date unknown15.

    • Shield of Protection is called "the most essential stigma," taken first to Lv 5 or 10 instead, Nezakan's Shield second inven 167, date unknown16
    • Both sources agree these two form the core pair, disagreeing only on order
  5. Lv 25
    Push both basics to skill Lv 12

    One source ties this to about character Lv 25, the only step pinned to a specific character level inven 93, date unknown17.

  6. Lv 25-45
    Layer Stigmas as timed defensive cooldowns

    Use Shield of Protection and/or Nezakan's Shield against confirmed incoming damage, not on cooldown inven 167, date unknown18.

    • On trash pulls, cancel the left-click animation into a right-click or skill ("평캔") to keep damage cycling monotrees, date unknown19
  7. Lv 45-50
    Greater Stigma quest unlocks

    No reliable source names which Greater Stigma to take for Templar at this unlock.

  8. At cap
    Rotation shifts to dungeon-oriented group pulls

    Open with Capture, apply Weakness Strike, then alternate Guardian Strike with the basics monotrees, date unknown20.

    • On single-target bosses, cycle Provoke, Execution's Blade, and Divine Punishment, filling gaps with Annihilation and basics inven 104, date unknown21
    • See Skill priority above and Stigma picks below for the full endgame spread

Gear while leveling

  • Balance Damage Amplification, Critical Damage Amplification, Agility, and Block rating per slot rather than stacking pure offense vortexgaming, date unknown22
  • Prioritize Critical Strike race-understanding at slots 3 and 9, and Iron Wall Defense understanding at slot 6 vortexgaming, date unknown23

No source gives a Templar leveling-specific weapon-swap schedule; this is general itemization guidance, not level-tied.

Two sources disagree on the Lv 23 stigma pick: Nezakan's Shield first for survivability monotrees, date unknown24 vs. Shield of Protection first as "the most essential stigma" inven 167, date unknown25. A separate, unverified snippet describes an older 8/10/12 specialization-breakpoint order rather than the 8/12/16 model used above (single unverified source, no direct link).
Avoid: over-investing in Capture, Shock Release, and Annihilation; multiple sources call these low-value against the core rotation inven 130, 2025-1126 dcinside, 2026-0727.

blocks.title: Stigma picks
blocks.bodyHtml:
Stigmas unlock at level 23; build Templar's toward defense, taunt range, and self-healing.

System basics (cross-class, confirmed)

  • Stigmas unlock around level 23 aion2hub, date unknown1
  • A "Greater" stigma tier unlocks via group quests around level 45 to 50 single source aion2hub, date unknown2
    • Elyos get "[Group] The Shattered Stigma" from Miriya in Sanctum's Protector's Hall
    • Asmodians get "[Group] The Shulak's Stigma" from Vergelmir in Pandaemonium
  • Normal Stigma Skills level to 20 with Stigma Shards, then continue past 20 with higher-tier Advanced Stigma Shards recovered on reset expcarry, date unknown3
  • kr-era The Korean service raised the max Stigma level from 20 to 25 and allows up to six Stigma Skills equipped at once; balance and UI may change before global launch expcarry, date unknown4

PvE build focus

single source, marketing-adjacent aggregator The clearest PvE framing found for Templar stigma picks: build for Defensive Cooldowns, Taunt Range/Duration, and Self-Healing/HP Regeneration rather than damage.

  • Double Armor boosts resistance and reflects damage to nearby enemies on large pulls; Vampiric Sword gives a burst heal plus damage for emergencies noping, date unknown5

Other framing (no stigma names given)

single source, build-aggregator, no stigma names A second, less detailed source frames the choice as stat priorities rather than named stigmas:

  • PvE tanking: Defense/HP/Block plus guard or taunt skills
  • PvP tanking: Damage Defense/HP/Block/Evasion plus self-protect stigmas
  • Both paired with Justice or Life(/Space) Pantheon domains aion2hub builds, date unknown6
Gap remains: no KR-language source naming specific 템플러/수호성 stigmas by name was found; a Korean search returned other classes' stigma threads instead. Still no reliable KR-side confirmation of exact stigma names or priority order, so the two picks above (Double Armor, Vampiric Sword) are the best documented names available, not a confirmed full list.

What to spend Stigma Shards on first: whichever mitigation, taunt, or self-heal skill you have slotted and use every pull. This matches the Defensive Cooldown/Taunt/Self-Healing framing above and the general cross-class guidance to fund whatever you actually have equipped expcarry, date unknown7.

blocks.title: Daevanion board route
blocks.headExtrasHtml: single source, general mechanics only kr-era
blocks.bodyHtml:
Boards unlock at levels 12, 20, 30, 40, and four level-45 boards; no confirmed Templar-specific route yet.

Board unlock levels (confirmed, cross-class)

  • confirmed, general mechanic Nezekan (Lv 12), Zikel (Lv 20), Vaizel (Lv 30), Triniel (Lv 40), and four level-45 advanced boards: Ariel, Azphel, Marchutan, and Yustiel fextralife, date unknown1
  • kr-era, single source A Korean gaming-news piece corroborates the same unlock levels and adds stat themes per board daum news, 2025-112
    • Nezekan: combat speed and cooldown reduction
    • Zikel: damage amplification and resistance
    • Vaizel: critical damage amplification and resistance
    • Triniel: multi-hit accuracy and resistance

Neither source gives a Templar-specific route through these boards.

Gap remains: still no reliable source for a Templar-specific Daevanion route, which nodes, blue active-skill nodes vs green passive nodes vs stat nodes, or a node-by-node path within the boards above.

How the board works

Daevanion Points buy connected nodes on a board; nodes either add flat combat stats or add levels to specific skills. Points come from normal character leveling plus Daevanion Crystals earned through quests and achievements expcarry, date unknown3.

Strategy: trace the shortest legal path to the node that actually helps your build. Treat small connector nodes as a toll, not a destination, and match node choice, skill vs stat, to what your loadout needs most.

kr-era Reset: the Korean client supports resetting the whole board or eligible individual nodes, with individual resets costing 500 Kinah in KR, and a dependency rule that a node cannot be removed while another already-acquired node depends on it; cost may differ at global launch expcarry, date unknown4.

When to reset: no Templar-specific guidance was found; general advice implies resetting once your loadout changes enough that current nodes no longer serve it.

blocks.title: Arcana
blocks.bodyHtml:
No confirmed Arcana list for Templar; chase HP%, Defense, and Shield Block Rate regardless of set.

Two competing Arcana set recommendations turned up for Templar. Both are single source via search synthesis with no directly fetchable article, date unknown.

Vigor 4 / Purity 4

  • Grail and Parchment slotted as Vigor
  • Compass, Bell, Mirror, and Scales slotted as Purity

Search synthesis, no direct source link found, date unknown.

Vigor / Magic / Purity mix

  • For players with existing pieces
  • Grail and Parchment as Vigor, Bell and Mirror as Magic, Compass and Scales as Purity

Search synthesis, no direct source link found, date unknown.

Core stats

single source Chase these on Templar Arcana regardless of set, same search synthesis, date unknown:

  • HP%
  • Defense
  • Shield Block Rate

General framing: a card that is best for a boss-DPS build can be mediocre for a tank holding difficult content, so pick Arcana around the job you are actually doing rather than a generic "best" card.

For newer players still building out Key and Hourglass Arcana specifically, a 4-piece Punishment plus 4-piece Guardian setup is cited as giving a 5% Weapon Damage Amplification bonus, with the advice to upgrade Keys before Hourglasses single source mmoexp, date unknown1.

Avoid over-trusting this one: that Key/Hourglass framing reads generic rather than Templar-specific, so treat it with caution.
No reliable source found naming specific Arcana cards Templar should avoid.

blocks.title: Gear and stat priority
blocks.bodyHtml:
Use a sword or mace plus shield; stack Defense, HP, Block Rate, and damage reduction.

One-handed sword or mace plus shield is the default weapon. Several shield skills reportedly require a shield equipped, so sword/mace vs. greatsword comes down to preference once you commit to shield skills single source fextralife, date unknown1.

Aion 1 data, not AION 2: the advice that sword-vs-mace depends on whether your stigmas are magical, and that you should "get your weapon before your armor," traces back to aion.fandom.com/wiki/Templar, which documents the original 2009 Aion, not AION 2. This is legacy-game information of uncertain relevance, not confirmed AION 2 fact aion.fandom (Aion 1)2.

Stat priority

Stat priority actually documented for AION 2 Templar:

  1. Do first: Defense single source pvpbank-style synthesis3.
  2. Do first: HP pvpbank-style synthesis4.
  3. Then: Block Rate pvpbank-style synthesis5.
  4. Then: general damage reduction, called out alongside the above as the critical survivability stats pvpbank-style synthesis6.

Enhancement order (general, KR-era)

single source, KR-era, general not Templar-exclusive A KR guide on item-level growth strategy, used by Templar players in community threads, gives this order:

  1. Weapon first, for the biggest felt impact on combat
  2. Guard/chest slot and accessories next
  3. Armor pieces (gloves, body, boots) enhanced steadily for long-term use starting mid-progression

It separately flags Daevanion, the Amulet of Revelation (계시의 아뮬렛), and the Belt of Nobility (고결의 허리띠) as the three biggest early item-level gains to prioritize lifefin.co.kr, date unknown7.

Gap remains: the order above is general, not Templar-exclusive, so treat it as directional. No fully Templar-specific slot-by-slot enhancement order was found. The general guidance, from Gladiator sources and likely applicable directionally to any melee class, agrees that weapon upgrades tend to be prioritized before armor early on, because weapon level affects threat generation and base output even for a tank aion2wiki, date unknown8.

No AION 2-specific manastone or godstone terminology was found in any source. AION 2 appears to use the Arcana system (cards, Key, Hourglass) described above in place of AION 1's manastone/godstone slotting, but no source explicitly confirmed this mapping.

No reliable source found for a direct Templar armor set effect.

blocks.title: Rotation and combos
blocks.headExtrasHtml: confirmed pattern, contested order kr-era marketing
blocks.bodyHtml:
Chain Vicious Strike into Provoke, save Doom Shield for confirmed burst, pull adds with Capture.

Beginner PvE rotation

  1. Chain Vicious Strike to build and hold threat.
  2. Lock the primary target with Provoke.
  3. Time Doom Shield or other damage-reduction cooldowns specifically against confirmed incoming boss burst, rather than on cooldown.
  4. Follow up locked-down or staggered targets with Punishment and Decisive Strike for your hardest hits aion2hub, date unknown1 aoeah, 2025-112.

Multi-target pulls

Use Capture to drag scattered adds into a cluster, then use Trial (Falling Sword Spirits) or Shield Strike to hit the whole pack at once. Both scale their return, defense shred or healing, with the number of enemies hit single source (community synthesis, no direct link)

Aggro and defensive cooldowns

  • Mix Provoke and what one source calls "God's Punishment" alternately rather than spamming a single taunt; relying on one taunt skill is cited as a common way to lose aggro on mixed mob/boss pulls single source, unconfirmed skill name
  • Reserve big shields and damage-reduction cooldowns for confirmed mechanics, telegraphed boss bursts, instead of using them defensively on cooldown or reactively after damage has already landed single source
No reliable source found documenting an auto-hunt or macro skill setup specifically for Templar. Gladiator sources document a macro setup; nothing equivalent turned up for Templar.

blocks.title: Leveling notes
blocks.headExtrasHtml: single source kr-era marketing
blocks.bodyHtml:
Templar levels at a moderate pace: tough and self-sufficient, but not a fast solo killer.

  • Solo comfort: strong self-sustain via lifesteal (Bloodsword Slash), shields that heal based on hits landed, and CC/pulls via Capture make it survivable and good against larger mob groups
  • Trade-off: low personal damage next to Gladiator, Assassin, and Sorcerer means clear speed and leveling pace can feel slow, especially with an unoptimized gear or skill setup pvpbank, date unknown1

Sustain and mob density

  • Sustain comes primarily from damage-to-healing conversion, Bloodsword Slash heals 100% of damage dealt off Flash Cut procs, and shields that scale with enemies hit, not from potions or mana regen pvpbank, date unknown2
  • Handles larger mob groups comfortably thanks to its AoE pull (Capture) and multi-target defense and heal skills (Trial, Shield Strike): "win through consistency and battlefield control rather than burst" pvpbank, date unknown3

When the class "turns on": sources consistently flag gear, mastery investment, and defensive-stat itemization as having an outsized impact on Templar performance, more so than for most other classes. The class feels notably better once gear catches up rather than being strong purely from base kit pvpbank, date unknown4.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.headExtrasHtml: mostly single source marketing
blocks.bodyHtml:
Play actively, save cooldowns for real bursts, and do not expect Gladiator-level clear speed.

  1. Playing statically instead of actively repositioning; sources note the class rewards active tactical positioning and constant movement, not passive tanking single source.
  2. Using big defensive cooldowns like Doom Shield reactively or on cooldown instead of saving them for confirmed, telegraphed boss burst windows single source.
  3. Relying on a single taunt skill on mixed pulls instead of alternating taunts, cited as a cause of lost aggro single source.
  4. Underestimating how gear, mastery, and defensive-stat dependent the class is, and under-investing in upgrades relative to other classes pvpbank, date unknown1.
  5. Neglecting weapon upgrades in favor of armor only, when weapon level affects threat generation and the class's already-low DPS. Directional caution only, sourced from legacy Aion 1 Templar wiki content, not confirmed for AION 2 aion.fandom (Aion 1)2.
  6. Expecting Gladiator, Assassin, or Sorcerer-level solo clear speed and getting frustrated, instead of leaning into the control and durability playstyle the class is built around pvpbank, date unknown3.
  7. Not consolidating scattered mobs with Capture before using AoE mitigation or heal skills, losing out on the healing-per-target-hit scaling those skills offer single source.
  8. Skipping general new-player fundamentals: learning combat and movement before spending scarce upgrade materials applies to Templar as much as any class aion2wiki, date unknown4.
